slot.brief: Evaluate statements on gold number, protective action of lyophilic sols, and Hardy–Schulze rule for coagulation; pick the incorrect one.

stem: Select the incorrect statement about protective colloids and coagulation.
options: A larger gold number indicates greater protective action.
The gold number is the mass in milligrams of a protective colloid needed to protect 10 mL of a gold sol against coagulation by 1 mL of 10% NaCl solution.
Lyophilic sols can protect lyophobic sols by forming a protective layer around their particles.
By the Hardy–Schulze rule, coagulating power increases with the valency of the oppositely charged ion.

verdicts.working: A, C, and D are correct. A smaller gold number means greater protective action, so B is incorrect.

working:
Gold number $

\propto$ inverse of protective power.

Hence statement B is incorrect.

Independent check: A, C, and D are correct. A smaller gold number means greater protective action, so B is incorrect.
solution: Gold number is inversely proportional to protective power: a smaller gold number means greater protective action. Hence statement (A), which claims the opposite, is incorrect.
